title: Little Red Riding Hood (Rotkäppchen)

full_text:
Once upon a time, there was a sweet little village girl who was loved by everyone who looked at her, but most of all by her grandmother, who gave her a little cape of red velvet. It suited her so well that she would wear nothing else, and so she was called Little Red Riding Hood (Rotkäppchen).

One morning, her mother said: "Here, Little Red Riding Hood, take this cake and bottle of wine to your grandmother; she is weak and ill, and they will do her good. Walk nicely and quietly along the path, and do not stray into the forest, or you might fall and break the bottle!"

"I will take great care," promised the little girl.

The grandmother lived half an hour's walk away in the deep oak forest. When Red Riding Hood entered the woods, a wolf met her. The child did not know what a wicked beast he was, and was not afraid of him.

"Good day, Little Red Riding Hood!" said the wolf softly.
"Good day, wolf!"
"Where are you going so early?"
"To grandmother's, to take her fresh cake and wine."
"Where does grandmother live?"
"Under the three large oak trees near the hazel hedge," said the innocent child.

The wolf thought: "What a tender, juicy morsel! She will taste even sweeter than the old woman!" He pointed to the sunny glade: "Look at the lovely bluebells and yellow buttercups! Why don't you gather a fresh bouquet for your grandmother?"

Red Riding Hood thought: "A fresh bouquet will bring grandmother joy!" She left the path and wandered among the flowers, running from one bloom to the next.

Meanwhile, the wolf ran straight to the grandmother's cottage, knocked on the door, and spoke in a disguised voice: "It is Little Red Riding Hood with cake and wine!"

"Press the latch, my dear!" called the grandmother from her bed.

The wolf leaped in, swallowed the poor old grandmother whole, put on her nightgown and frilly nightcap, drew the bed-curtains, and lay down in the bed.

When Red Riding Hood had gathered as many flowers as she could carry, she ran to the cottage. Finding the door open, she felt an eerie dread. She entered the bedroom:
"Good morning, grandmother!" but received no answer. She drew the curtains.

"Oh, grandmother, what big ears you have!"
"The better to hear you with, my child!"
"Oh, grandmother, what big eyes you have!"
"The better to see you with!"
"Oh, grandmother, what big hands you have!"
"The better to hug you with!"
"Oh, but grandmother, what a terrible big mouth you have!"
"The better to eat you with!"

The wolf leaped from the bed and swallowed poor Little Red Riding Hood whole! Having satisfied his appetite, the beast lay down again and fell into a loud, snoring sleep.

A brave huntsman passed the house, thinking: "How loudly the old woman snores! I must see if she needs aid."

Peering through the window, he saw the wolf lying in the bed! "Have I found you at last, old sinner?" said the huntsman. He raised his rifle, but thought: "Perhaps the beast has swallowed the grandmother whole, and she may yet be saved!"

He took a pair of heavy shears and carefully snipped open the sleeping wolf's belly. After a few cuts, a little red cape gleamed forth! Out stepped Little Red Riding Hood, crying: "Oh, how dark and terrifying it was inside the wolf!" Then the old grandmother came out alive, though scarcely able to breathe.

Red Riding Hood gathered heavy field stones, with which they filled the wolf's belly, sewing it up neatly. When the wolf woke and tried to leap up to flee, the heavy stones dragged him down, and he collapsed dead upon the floor.

The huntsman took the wolf's pelt, the grandmother ate the cake and drank the wine, and Little Red Riding Hood thought: "Never again in my life will I stray from the path when my mother has forbidden it!"
moral: Disobeying wise counsel and straying from the honest path invites dangerous predators.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Little Red Riding Hood (Rotkäppchen)"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.

the ability to judge well and understand the truth

discussion_questions.prompt: What is the main situation at the beginning of "Little Red Riding Hood (Rotkäppchen)"?

How could you use this lesson in your own school or family life?
Was the character’s final decision fair and kind to everyone?
Imagine an alternate peaceful ending or a new creative adventure for these characters.

reflection_prompt: Have you ever had to choose between acting quickly in anger or waiting patiently to understand the truth?
